title: Getting Started with rladybugdb
text: rladybugdb provides R interface LadybugDB, embedded columnar graph database uses openCypher query language. LadybugDB fork KuzuDB supports Cypher dialect. Starting v0.2.0 package uses native Rcpp C++ bindings compiled LadybugDB C library (liblbug). C library bundled package — Python, reticulate, extra installation step required.
code: R → Rcpp (rladybugdb.so) → C API (lbug.h) → LadybugDB engine

title: Getting Started with rladybugdb
text: Install GitHub: configure script downloads prebuilt liblbug binary platform install time. package fully self-contained. Verify library working: Note: ladybugdb_install() deprecated longer anything. need call .
code: # install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("hadimaster65555/rladybugdb") library(rladybugdb) ladybugdb_version()      # e.g. "0.15.2" #> [1] "0.15.2" ladybugdb_is_installed() # TRUE #> [1] TRUE

title: Getting Started with rladybugdb
text: lb_database() opens creates LadybugDB database. Pass ":memory:" transient -memory database (ideal testing interactive exploration): persistent -disk database pass directory path: Use lb_close() release resources done:
code: library(rladybugdb)  db   <- lb_database(":memory:") conn <- lb_connection(db) db #> <lb_database> path=:memory: read_only=FALSE conn #> <lb_connection> db=:memory: db <- lb_database("~/my_graph_db") lb_close(conn) lb_close(db)

title: Getting Started with rladybugdb
text: LadybugDB uses property graph model: nodes belong node tables edges belong relationship tables. defined Cypher DDL:
code: # Node tables lb_execute(conn, "CREATE NODE TABLE Person (   name   STRING,   age    INT64,   PRIMARY KEY (name) )") #> <lb_result> [1 x 1] #>                           result #> 1 Table Person has been created.  lb_execute(conn, "CREATE NODE TABLE City (   name    STRING,   country STRING,   PRIMARY KEY (name) )") #> <lb_result> [1 x 1] #>                         result #> 1 Table City has been created.  # Relationship table (directed: Person → City) lb_execute(conn, "CREATE REL TABLE LivesIn (FROM Person TO City, since INT64)") #> <lb_result> [1 x 1] #>                            result #> 1 Table LivesIn has been created.

title: Getting Started with rladybugdb
code: lb_execute(conn, "CREATE (:Person {name: 'Alice', age: 30})") #> <lb_result> (no columns) lb_execute(conn, "CREATE (:Person {name: 'Bob',   age: 25})") #> <lb_result> (no columns) lb_execute(conn, "CREATE (:City   {name: 'London', country: 'UK'})") #> <lb_result> (no columns) lb_execute(conn, "CREATE (:City   {name: 'Paris',  country: 'France'})") #> <lb_result> (no columns)  lb_execute(conn, "   MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Alice'}), (c:City {name: 'London'})   CREATE (p)-[:LivesIn {since: 2018}]->(c) ") #> <lb_result> (no columns) lb_execute(conn, "   MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Bob'}), (c:City {name: 'Paris'})   CREATE (p)-[:LivesIn {since: 2021}]->(c) ") #> <lb_result> (no columns)

what: Bulk loading from an R data frame
title: Getting Started with rladybugdb
text: larger datasets lb_copy_from_df() writes data frame temporary CSV uses LadybugDB’s COPY … loader — much faster individual CREATE statements:
code: more_people <- data.frame(   name = c("Carol", "Dave"),   age  = c(35L,     28L) ) lb_copy_from_df(conn, more_people, "Person") #> <lb_result> [1 x 1] #>                                           result #> 1 2 tuples have been copied to the Person table.  lb_query(conn, "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name, p.age AS age ORDER BY p.name") #>    name age #> 1 Alice  30 #> 2   Bob  25 #> 3 Carol  35 #> 4  Dave  28

title: Getting Started with rladybugdb
code: lb_copy_from_csv(conn, "/data/people.csv", "Person")

what: lb_query() — query directly to a data frame
title: Getting Started with rladybugdb
code: df <- lb_query(conn,   "MATCH (p:Person)-[:LivesIn]->(c:City)    RETURN p.name AS person, c.name AS city, c.country AS country    ORDER BY p.name") df #>   person   city country #> 1  Alice London      UK #> 2    Bob  Paris  France

title: Getting Started with rladybugdb
text: lb_result holds lazy cursor. Convert explicitly:
code: result <- lb_execute(conn,   "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name, p.age AS age ORDER BY p.age") result          # prints column schema #> <lb_result> [4 x 2] #>    name age #> 1   Bob  25 #> 2  Dave  28 #> 3 Alice  30 #> 4 Carol  35 as.data.frame(result) #>   name age #> 1 <NA>  NA #> 2 <NA>  NA #> 3 <NA>  NA #> 4 <NA>  NA

title: Getting Started with rladybugdb
text: Use named parameters (prefixed $) instead string interpolation. avoids Cypher-injection bugs handles type coercion automatically: Supported parameter types: character, integer, double, logical.
code: lb_execute(conn,   "MATCH (p:Person {name: $name}) RETURN p.age AS age",   parameters = list(name = "Alice")) #> <lb_result> [1 x 1] #>   age #> 1  30

title: Getting Started with rladybugdb
code: result <- lb_execute(conn,   "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name, p.age AS age ORDER BY p.age") tibble::as_tibble(result) #> # A tibble: 4 × 2 #>   name    age #>   <chr> <dbl> #> 1 Bob      25 #> 2 Dave     28 #> 3 Alice    30 #> 4 Carol    35

title: Getting Started with rladybugdb
code: result <- lb_execute(conn,   "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name, p.age AS age") as_arrow_table(result) #> Table #> 4 rows x 2 columns #> $name <string> #> $age <double> #>  #> See $metadata for additional Schema metadata

title: Getting Started with rladybugdb
text: query returns full node relationship columns (.e. RETURN p, r, c rather individual properties), as_igraph() as_tbl_graph() convert result graph objects.
code: result <- lb_execute(conn,   "MATCH (p:Person)-[r:LivesIn]->(c:City) RETURN p, r, c") g <- as_igraph(result) print(g) #> IGRAPH f0871c8 DN-- 4 2 --  #> + attr: name (v/c), _LABEL (v/c), age (v/n), country (v/c), _LABEL #> | (e/c), since (e/n) #> + edges from f0871c8 (vertex names): #> [1] Alice->London Bob  ->Paris result2 <- lb_execute(conn,   "MATCH (p:Person)-[r:LivesIn]->(c:City) RETURN p, r, c") tg <- as_tbl_graph(result2) tg #> # A tbl_graph: 4 nodes and 2 edges #> # #> # A rooted forest with 2 trees #> # #> # Node Data: 4 × 4 (active) #>   name   `_LABEL`   age country #>   <chr>  <chr>    <dbl> <chr>   #> 1 Alice  Person      30 NA      #> 2 Bob    Person      25 NA      #> 3 London City        NA UK      #> 4 Paris  City        NA France  #> # #> # Edge Data: 2 × 4 #>    from    to `_LABEL` since #>   <int> <int> <chr>    <dbl> #> 1     1     3 LivesIn   2018 #> 2     2     4 LivesIn   2021

title: Real-world graph analysis: OpenFlights
text: OpenFlights publishes two CSV files: airports routes. download temporary directory start session.
code: library(rladybugdb) suppressPackageStartupMessages({   library(ggplot2)   library(dplyr) })  base_url     <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpatokal/openflights/master/data" airports_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "airports.dat") routes_file   <- file.path(tempdir(), "routes.dat")  download.file(paste0(base_url, "/airports.dat"), airports_file, quiet = TRUE) download.file(paste0(base_url, "/routes.dat"),   routes_file,   quiet = TRUE)

title: Real-world graph analysis: OpenFlights
text: raw files comma-separated header row. assign column names manually filter real airports valid IATA code coordinates. filtering roughly 6 200 airports 63 000 routes.
code: airports_raw <- read.csv(airports_file, header = FALSE, quote = '"',                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = c("", "\\N"),                          col.names = c("id","name","city","country","iata","icao",                                        "lat","lng","alt","tz","dst","tz_name","type","source"))  routes_raw <- read.csv(routes_file, header = FALSE, quote = '"',                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = c("", "\\N"),                        col.names = c("airline","airline_id","src_iata","src_id",                                      "dst_iata","dst_id","codeshare","stops","equipment"))  # Keep only real airports with valid coordinates and IATA codes airports <- airports_raw |>   filter(type == "airport", nchar(iata) == 3,          !is.na(lat), !is.na(lng), !is.na(id)) |>   transmute(     id      = as.integer(id),     name    = name,     city    = city,     country = country,     iata    = iata,     lat     = as.double(lat),     lng     = as.double(lng),     alt     = as.integer(ifelse(is.na(alt), 0L, as.integer(alt)))   )  # Keep routes where both endpoints reference known airports known_ids <- airports$id routes <- routes_raw |>   filter(!is.na(src_id), !is.na(dst_id),          suppressWarnings(!is.na(as.integer(src_id))),          suppressWarnings(!is.na(as.integer(dst_id)))) |>   transmute(     src_id  = as.integer(src_id),     dst_id  = as.integer(dst_id),     airline = ifelse(is.na(airline), "Unknown", airline),     stops   = as.integer(ifelse(is.na(stops), 0L, stops))   ) |>   filter(src_id %in% known_ids, dst_id %in% known_ids, src_id != dst_id)

title: Real-world graph analysis: OpenFlights
text: model airports nodes routes directed edges. graph schema uses one node table (Airport) one relationship table (Route). lb_copy_from_df() uses LadybugDB’s native bulk loader, orders magnitude faster row--row CREATE statements:
code: db   <- lb_database(":memory:") conn <- lb_connection(db)  lb_execute(conn, "   CREATE NODE TABLE Airport (     id      INT64,     name    STRING,     city    STRING,     country STRING,     iata    STRING,     lat     DOUBLE,     lng     DOUBLE,     alt     INT64,     PRIMARY KEY(id)   )")  lb_execute(conn, "   CREATE REL TABLE Route (     FROM Airport TO Airport,     airline STRING,     stops   INT64   )") lb_copy_from_df(conn, airports, "Airport") lb_copy_from_df(conn, routes,   "Route")

title: Real-world graph analysis: OpenFlights
text: Simple aggregate Cypher queries confirm data loaded correctly:
code: lb_query(conn, "   MATCH (a:Airport)   RETURN count(a) AS total_airports")  lb_query(conn, "   MATCH ()-[r:Route]->()   RETURN count(r) AS total_routes")

title: Real-world graph analysis: OpenFlights
text: airports outbound routes? aggregate count(), filter airports 10 routes, take top 30:  Frankfurt (FRA), London Heathrow (LHR), Charles de Gaulle (CDG) dominate top list, reflecting role major intercontinental connecting hubs.
code: top_hubs <- lb_query(conn, "   MATCH (a:Airport)-[r:Route]->()   WITH a.iata AS iata, a.name AS name, a.country AS country,        a.lat AS lat, a.lng AS lng, count(r) AS routes   WHERE routes > 10   RETURN iata, name, country, lat, lng, routes   ORDER BY routes DESC   LIMIT 30") p1 <- top_hubs |>   mutate(label = paste0(iata, "\n", sub(" International.*", "", name))) |>   ggplot(aes(x = reorder(label, routes), y = routes, fill = routes)) +   geom_col(width = 0.7) +   scale_fill_gradient(low = "#4da6ff", high = "#003380", guide = "none") +   coord_flip() +   labs(title = "Top 30 Airport Hubs — Outbound Routes",        subtitle = "Source: OpenFlights  |  LadybugDB graph query",        x = NULL, y = "Number of outbound routes") +   theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +   theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

title: Real-world graph analysis: OpenFlights
text: United States leads wide margin, followed Russia Canada — reflection large geographic size many regional airports.
code: by_country <- lb_query(conn, "   MATCH (a:Airport)   WITH a.country AS country, count(a) AS n_airports   RETURN country, n_airports   ORDER BY n_airports DESC   LIMIT 20")

title: Real-world graph analysis: OpenFlights
text: produce world map sample 3 000 route segments overlay top hub locations:  density routes across North Atlantic within North America Europe immediately visible. relative scarcity routes across South Pacific also striking.
code: route_map <- lb_query(conn, "   MATCH (src:Airport)-[r:Route]->(dst:Airport)   WHERE src.lng IS NOT NULL AND dst.lng IS NOT NULL   RETURN src.lat AS src_lat, src.lng AS src_lng,          dst.lat AS dst_lat, dst.lng AS dst_lng,          src.country AS country   LIMIT 3000")

title: Real-world graph analysis: OpenFlights
text: extract one-hop neighbourhood Frankfurt (FRA) — airports reachable direct Lufthansa partner flight — visualise network graph using ggraph:  Gold = Frankfurt hub, blue = European destinations, red = intercontinental destinations. hub--spoke structure clearly visible.
code: hub_net <- lb_query(conn, "   MATCH (src:Airport {iata: 'FRA'})-[r:Route]->(dst:Airport)   RETURN src.iata AS src, dst.iata AS dst,          dst.name AS dst_name, dst.country AS dst_country,          dst.lat AS dst_lat, dst.lng AS dst_lng,          r.airline AS airline   LIMIT 80") library(igraph) library(ggraph)  vertices <- data.frame(   name    = unique(c("FRA", hub_net$dst)),   country = c("Germany",                hub_net$dst_country[match(unique(hub_net$dst), hub_net$dst)]),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  europe <- c("Germany","France","United Kingdom","Spain","Italy","Netherlands",             "Switzerland","Austria","Belgium","Poland","Sweden","Norway",             "Denmark","Finland","Portugal","Greece","Czech Republic","Romania",             "Hungary","Ireland","Croatia","Slovakia","Bulgaria","Serbia")  edges_ig <- hub_net |> count(src, dst, name = "weight") g <- graph_from_data_frame(edges_ig, directed = TRUE, vertices = vertices) V(g)$region <- ifelse(V(g)$name == "FRA", "Hub",                 ifelse(V(g)$country %in% europe, "Europe", "Intercontinental"))

text: R interface LadybugDB — embedded columnar graph database Cypher queries.  rladybugdb provides native Rcpp binding LadybugDB C library. Python, reticulate, runtime setup — C library ships package loaded automatically library(rladybugdb). LadybugDB fork KuzuDB supports openCypher query dialect.

text: prebuilt LadybugDB C library downloaded automatically R CMD INSTALL via configure script (macOS/Linux) configure.win (Windows). setup needed.
code: # install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("hadimaster65555/rladybugdb") library(rladybugdb) ladybugdb_version()   # "0.15.2"

title: rladybugdb — R interface to LadybugDB
code: library(rladybugdb)  # Open an in-memory graph (or pass a directory path for persistence) db   <- lb_database(":memory:") conn <- lb_connection(db)  # Define schema lb_execute(conn, "CREATE NODE TABLE Person (name STRING, age INT64, PRIMARY KEY(name))") lb_execute(conn, "CREATE NODE TABLE City   (name STRING, country STRING, PRIMARY KEY(name))") lb_execute(conn, "CREATE REL TABLE LivesIn (FROM Person TO City, since INT64)")  # Insert data lb_execute(conn, "CREATE (:Person {name: 'Alice', age: 30})") lb_execute(conn, "CREATE (:City   {name: 'London', country: 'UK'})") lb_execute(conn, "MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Alice'}), (c:City {name: 'London'})                   CREATE (p)-[:LivesIn {since: 2018}]->(c)")  # Query → data.frame lb_query(conn, "MATCH (p:Person)-[:LivesIn]->(c:City)                 RETURN p.name AS person, c.name AS city, p.age AS age") #>   person   city age #> 1  Alice London  30  lb_close(conn) lb_close(db)

title: Execute a Cypher query — lb_execute
text: Sends Cypher query string LadybugDB returns lb_result object. DDL DML statements (CREATE TABLE, CREATE, MERGE, …) result contains metadata; MATCH/RETURN contains rows.

code: lb_execute(conn, query, parameters = NULL)

title: Execute a Cypher query — lb_execute
text: conn lb_connection object lb_connection(). query single character string containing Cypher query. parameters named list query parameters parameterised queries. NULL (default) means parameters.

text: object class lb_result.

title: Execute a Cypher query — lb_execute
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ db   <- lb_database(":memory:") conn <- lb_connection(db) lb_execute(conn, "CREATE NODE TABLE Person (name STRING, PRIMARY KEY(name))") lb_execute(conn, "CREATE (:Person {name: $name})",            parameters = list(name = "Alice")) } # }

title: rladybugdb 0.2.0
text: Python/reticulate backend removed. ladybugdb_install() now deprecated nothing. Remove calls scripts.

title: rladybugdb 0.2.0
text: Native Rcpp C++ bindings LadybugDB C library (liblbug v0.15.2). Python runtime required — C library ships package. ladybugdb_version() returns version bundled C library. Parameterised queries via parameters list argument lb_execute() lb_query(). Use $name placeholders Cypher avoid injection bugs. as_arrow_table() generic zero-copy Arrow output lb_result. as_tbl_graph() converts query results directly tidygraph::tbl_graph.

title: rladybugdb 0.2.0
text: LIST / ARRAY columns now returned proper R list columns (one R list element per row) rather collapsed strings. DATE columns map Date; TIMESTAMP columns map POSIXct; INT64 values map double (exact 2^53, covers graph IDs). lb_copy_from_df() lb_copy_from_csv() use LadybugDB’s native bulk loader, orders magnitude faster row--row CREATE.
